Value truncation and verification functions for record values in workspace memory.

# Purpose
[`fd_funk_val_truncate`](<#fd_funk_val_truncate>) manages the value area of a `fd_funk_rec_t` record. It validates the input arguments when `FD_FUNK_HANDHOLDING` is enabled, then changes the record value size to `sz`. If `sz` is `0`, it flushes the current value with `fd_funk_val_flush` and returns success. If `sz` is larger than the current capacity in `rec->val_max`, it allocates a new buffer with `fd_alloc_malloc_at_least`, copies the existing value, clears the unused tail, updates the record to point to the new workspace address, and frees the old buffer. If `sz` fits in the current allocation, it only updates `rec->val_sz` and returns the current local address from the workspace. The function reports errors through `opt_err` and uses `FD_FUNK_ERR_INVAL` or `FD_FUNK_ERR_MEM` when needed.

[`fd_funk_val_verify`](<#fd_funk_val_verify>) checks the value metadata for all records in a `fd_funk_t` instance. It walks every record with `fd_funk_all_iter_t` and verifies that `val_sz` does not exceed `val_max`, that `val_max` does not exceed `FD_FUNK_REC_VAL_MAX`, and that records with a nonzero `val_gaddr` also have a valid workspace tag that matches the `funk` workspace. This function returns `FD_FUNK_SUCCESS` when all records pass the checks, and `FD_FUNK_ERR_INVAL` when it finds an invalid value state.
